description: NumPy already releases the GIL. So threads should already pay off for your NumPy code, right? Christopher Ariza tested that. He summed the rows of a 10,000 by 10,000 array on Python 3.14. Sequential took 360 milliseconds. A thread pool took 373, slower than doing nothing. The same code on free- threaded Python 3.14t took 83.7 milliseconds. Free-threaded Python is officially supported as of 3.14. The GIL isn’t gone, though. It’s a zombie. Import one compiled package that hasn’t opted in, psycopg2 for example, and the GIL comes back for your entire process. You get a warning, not an error. Chris is the creator of StaticFrame and its C extension library ArrayKit. We dig into when threads beat plain NumPy, how to tell if you’re actually running free-threaded, and conditional-futures, his drop-in thread pool that stops your code from getting slower when the GIL wakes back up.
title: #570: Free-Threaded Python
